items.prompt:
What should you do if you come to a word you do not know while reading?
A) Skip it and keep going
B) Try to sound it out
C) Close the book
items.answer: B) Try to sound it out

steps: A good reader tries to decode an unknown word using phonics. Using context clues is also helpful.

items.prompt:
Which of these shows FLUENT reading?
A) 'The...dog...ran...fast.'
B) 'The dog ran fast.'

steps: Option B reads the words smoothly together. Option A is choppy word-by-word reading — not fluent.

items.prompt:
A period at the end of a sentence tells a reader to:
A) Speed up
B) Pause and stop
C) Read more quietly

steps: A period signals the end of a sentence. The reader pauses before starting the next sentence.

items.prompt:
Why do readers reread a sentence?
A) To check understanding
B) To get bored
C) To read fewer words

steps: Rereading helps a reader fix mistakes and understand the meaning better.

items.prompt:
A good reader reads with _____ to show feelings in the story.
A) expression
B) silence
C) speed only

steps: Reading with expression means using your voice to match the feeling of the text.

items.prompt:
A student reads a sentence and it does not make sense. What should she do?
A) Keep going without stopping
B) Go back and reread
C) Skip to the next page

steps: When reading does not make sense, a fluent reader goes back and rereads to self-correct.

items.prompt:
How should you read the sentence: 'Watch out!'?
A) Softly and slowly
B) With energy and loudness
C) In a flat, quiet voice

steps: The exclamation point (!) signals excitement or urgency. Read with energy.

items.prompt:
Reading too _____ makes it hard for others to understand you.
A) fast
B) slowly — but only sometimes
C) Both A and A apply

steps: Reading too fast can make words sound jumbled, making it hard to understand the meaning.

items.prompt:
A student reads 'She went to the store' correctly. This shows the student is reading with:
A) Accuracy
B) Slowness
C) Confusion

steps: Accuracy means reading the correct words. Reading the sentence correctly shows accuracy.

items.prompt:
What does a question mark at the end of a sentence tell you about how to read it?
A) Drop your voice
B) Raise your voice at the end
C) Shout loudly
items.answer: B) Raise your voice at the end

steps: A question mark (?) means the sentence is a question. Readers usually raise their voice slightly at the end.

items.prompt:
Which phrase shows a reader grouping words correctly while reading?
A) 'The / big / dog / ran / fast.'
B) 'The big dog / ran fast.'

steps: Fluent readers group words into meaningful phrases. Option B groups 'The big dog' and 'ran fast' — natural and meaningful.

items.prompt:
True or False: A fluent reader reads every single word perfectly on the very first try.
A) True
B) False

steps: Even fluent readers make occasional errors. What matters is that they notice mistakes and self-correct.

items.prompt:
A student reads the same book three times. Each time she reads it better. This is an example of:
A) Repeated reading for fluency practice
B) Reading too slowly
C) Giving up
items.answer: A) Repeated reading for fluency practice

steps: Re-reading familiar texts multiple times is a proven way to build fluency.

items.prompt:
The three parts of fluency are: accuracy, rate, and _____.
A) memorization
B) expression
C) spelling

steps: The three key parts of fluency are accuracy (correct words), rate (appropriate speed), and expression (voice and feeling).

items.prompt:
A reader reads: 'Sam likes his cat, Mittens.' She pauses slightly after 'cat'. Why?
A) She forgot the next word.
B) The comma tells her to pause briefly.
C) The sentence ended.
items.answer: B) The comma tells her to pause briefly.

steps: A comma signals a brief pause within a sentence. It does not end the sentence — it just creates a natural break.
